d1.title: D1. IoT in our sector: University of Birmingham
d1.text: Campus Lost & Found belongs to campus facilities within higher education. A real example is the University of Birmingham's partnership with Siemens: the university announced a rollout of 23,000 Enlighted IoT sensors, and Enlighted's case study describes installation in lighting fixtures [1,2]. Sensors collect energy consumption, occupancy, movement and temperature; Enlighted Manage analyses these readings to support decisions about room use and energy efficiency [2]. The manufacturer's documented architecture sends sensor data wirelessly over IEEE 802.15.4 to gateways, then over Ethernet/TCP/IP using TLS to Manage; this is a different wireless protocol from Wi-Fi [3]. Sensors also control lighting locally. Manage supports processing on a local server or in the cloud, although the campus sources do not identify which hosting option Birmingham uses [3]. The benefit is responsive lighting and better space planning, with campus data also supporting teaching and research [1,2]. One potential risk, in our assessment, is that detailed occupancy histories could expose people's routines if combined with other records. Restricting access, keeping aggregated reports and setting a retention limit would reduce that risk.

coverage.connectivity: Vendor-documented architecture: IEEE 802.15.4 wireless sensor-to-gateway links, then Ethernet/TCP/IP with TLS to Manage.
coverage.data: Energy consumption, occupancy, motion and temperature.
coverage.processing: Lighting control happens locally; Manage analyses sensor data. The product supports on-premises or cloud Manage, but the cited campus sources do not identify Birmingham's exact hosting choice.
coverage.benefit: Lighting and energy management, space-use decisions, and data for teaching and research.
coverage.risk: Our assessment: combining detailed occupancy histories with other records could expose routines; this is a potential risk, not an allegation of a breach.
